Mira Patel: FYI flagged a trial seat (BrightWave) hitting intermittent 429 + occasional 401s during their Node edge deploy. They said it started after scaling to ~60 RPS from Cloudflare workers. Can eng weigh in?
BrightWave Ops: yeah, started after we rolled v0.7.2 of the SDK into our edge functions. Symptoms: sudden 429s for ~30s windows then OK, and a few 401s that resolved without key rotation on our side. logs: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` and `x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 12` sometimes present.
Alex K.: thanks — can you paste a short request example (headers + small payload) and whether you send the API key from the worker or a backend proxy?
BrightWave Ops: sending directly from workers (serverless), key in env var at deploy time. snippet: ```fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-live-xxxx', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({model: 'redwood-2', prompt: 'hi'}) })```
Jamie Chen: @Alex K. @Mira Patel quick read: edge + shared key -> connection churn + many originated IPs -> our rate surface will see many short-lived clients. That can trigger our per-key burst policies. The transient 401s could be downstream proxy dropping Authorization on replays or an expired short-lived token if they're using any rotation.
Alex K.: two practical asks for BrightWave: 1) confirm whether workers reuse a single global keep-alive connection or create new TCP per request; 2) set debug headers enabled so we can see `x-rw-quota` and `x-rw-retry-after` when 429 happens.
BrightWave Ops: Cloudflare Workers uses fetch API; not persistent TCP. Hard to keep connections. We can try adding a tiny proxy on our origin though.
Mira Patel: for onboarding risk — they’re in trial. If we can get a short config suggestion (backoff/retry) + doc snippet they can implement today, should reduce renewal risk.
Jamie Chen: recommended pattern for serverless clients: 1) do NOT embed long-lived secret in client-side code; 2) run lightweight origin proxy (small server in VPC) that holds key and handles batching; 3) if proxy not possible, use scoped short-lived tokens via our token service (we can issue a scoped key limited to generation endpoints, TTL 1h). For immediate mitigation, implement exponential backoff with jitter and honoring `x-rw-retry-after` header. Example pseudocode: ```const backoff = (attempt) => Math.min(1000 * 2**attempt, 30000) + Math.floor(Math.random()*300); async function guardedFetch(attempt=0){ const res = await fetch(...); if(res.status===429){ const retry = res.headers.get('x-rw-retry-after'); await sleep(retry ? Number(retry)*1000 : backoff(attempt)); return guardedFetch(attempt+1); } return res; }```
Alex K.: also check for 401s — if they see `WWW-Authenticate` or `x-rw-auth-fail` we need logs. If token rotation is happening, make sure rotation handshake completes before new requests. Common pattern causing 401s: parallel requests during rotation using both old+new tokens.
BrightWave Ops: got it. We'll enable debug headers and add backoff wrapper. We can also try proxy but prefer to push scoped tokens first. Can you enable a short scoped token for trial for us to test?
Mira Patel: I can create a scoped test key with 1h TTL. @Jamie Chen can you approve?
Jamie Chen: approved. I’ll generate `test-scope-brightwave-2026` and drop it into the thread once created. Also pinging CS Bot to record a follow-up.
CS Bot: Follow-up created: #cs-followups-4723 assigned to Mira Patel, due 2026-03-24.
BrightWave Ops: testing now — initial results: reduced 429s, 401s gone. We'll keep you posted over next 24h. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Mira Patel: marking onboarding health as "at risk -> monitoring" until 24h window passes. If they still have jittering we'll schedule an enablement call to help add a lightweight proxy.
Alex K.: if they need a quick proxy example, I'll paste a tiny express snippet (one-liner cache + forward) in the follow-up doc.
BrightWave Ops: perfect, appreciate the quick turnaround.
